chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Abi Umayr from Ja'far ibn 'Uthman said:

My father carried goods to Syria with a carrier (carrier of goods), and he mentioned that a load from them was lost. I mentioned this to Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), and he said, 'Do you accuse him?' I said, 'No.' He said, 'Then do not make him liable for compensation (guarantee him for the loss).'

key_terms.تُضَمِّنْهُ: Make him liable / guarantee him (for compensation)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a carrier's liability for lost goods in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the default liability status of a hired carrier (karram), establishing that loss of goods does not automatically imply negligence unless the owner explicitly accuses the carrier of fault. It highlights the Shia legal principle of 'al-asl al-bara'a' (presumption of innocence) in commercial contracts, distinguishing between mere loss and actionable breach of trust. This ruling protects carriers from arbitrary claims, ensuring that financial responsibility is tied to proven misconduct rather than the mere occurrence of loss.
